      "subject": "Re: the apartment viewing on Saturday – final tenancy details",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

Thank you for sending the signed tenancy agreement and standing-order confirmation. I’ve checked both, and everything is now in place following your viewing of the apartment on Saturday, 14 September.

To confirm the figures one final time, the monthly rent for Flat 3, 18 Mill Lane is £925, payable on the first working day of each month. Your first payment will be the agreed pro-rata amount of £462.50 for 16–30 September. I’ve also received the £1,067.30 deposit by bank transfer; it will be registered with the Deposit Protection Service within 30 days of receipt, and I’ll forward the certificate and prescribed information as soon as they issue them. No other administration or holding fee is due.

I have countersigned the document titled “Assured Shorthold Tenancy Agreement – 18 Mill Lane – 16 September” and attached the completed copy, together with the final Inventory and Schedule of Condition. I added the two points we discussed after Saturday’s viewing: the small mark on the bedroom windowsill and the loose handle on the cupboard beneath the kitchen sink. The handle is being repaired tomorrow, but I have left the note in the inventory so there is a complete record. The gas-safety certificate, electrical installation report, EPC and current How to Rent guide are included in the same attachment bundle.

Key collection is confirmed for Monday, 16 September at 17:30 at the apartment. As you mentioned that you may be coming directly from the river station, there is no problem if traffic makes you a few minutes late; just text me when you leave. I’ll bring two building-entry fobs, two sets of apartment keys and one mailbox key. We can take the opening meter readings together and sign the inventory acknowledgement then. If your gauge-maintenance call-out runs over and you cannot make 17:30, I can wait until 18:30, or leave the keys with Daniel in the ground-floor office once I have checked your photo ID in person.

The water account remains with Severn Regional Water, while electricity is currently supplied by Green Current Energy. You are free to change the electricity supplier after the tenancy begins. Council tax is Band B and should be transferred into your name from 16 September. Broadband is not included in the rent.

For completeness, your request to store your rescue-training kit in the locked basement cage is approved. The cage allocated to Flat 3 is marked “3B”; please keep wet ropes and buoyancy equipment in sealed tubs so the communal floor stays dry. Bicycles must remain in the rack rather than in the corridor.

Please reply only if any detail above differs from your understanding. Otherwise, I’ll see you at 17:30 on Monday with the keys and check-in sheet.

Best wishes,

Margaret Kendall
margaret.kendall@example.com

      "subject": "Re: the glaze firing schedule — revised kiln allocation for 18–23 June",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve updated the glaze firing schedule to reflect everything we agreed in your note yesterday. The revised document is attached as “Glaze_Firing_Schedule_v12_18-23_June.pdf”, along with the final shelf plan (“Kiln2_ShelfPlan_C.pdf”). Please disregard v11, particularly the Friday unloading times.

Your six river-stone bowls and the two tall gauge-marker vases are now booked into Kiln 2 for the cone 6 oxidation firing on Tuesday 18 June. Loading will start at 4:30 pm, with candling from 6:00 pm to midnight and the main programme beginning at 6:00 am on Wednesday. Based on the last run, the kiln should reach temperature at about 3:15 pm. We won’t crack the lid before 8:00 am Thursday 20 June, and collection is scheduled for 5:30–7:00 pm that evening.

I allowed 2.5 shelves for your work rather than the two shown in the earlier version. The marker vases need 55 mm clearance from the elements, and I’d rather not squeeze the bowls beneath them. Your estimated firing contribution is therefore $42.50, comprising $35 for shelf space and $7.50 toward the slow-cool programme. That replaces the $38 estimate from 11 June. No need to transfer it separately—I’ve added it to the shared studio invoice due 28 June.

I also moved the test tiles labelled RG-14, RG-15 and RG-16 to the Saturday 22 June firing. As you pointed out, RG-15 has the revised 80/20 iron wash, so it shouldn’t be used as the reference tile for the bowls in Tuesday’s load. I’ve marked RG-12 as the reference instead. Could you please check that the handwritten labels are still legible when you drop everything off?

For delivery, the side storeroom will be open from 3:45 pm on Tuesday. If the river-gauge inspection at Bellbird Crossing runs over, leave the two padded crates on the lower green rack and text me; I can wax the remaining foot rings before loading. Please don’t leave them outside the kiln room, as the Thursday class has clay deliveries arriving in the same corridor.

One other change: Priya has withdrawn her four platters, so there is room for your three small rescue-rope mugs if they are bone dry by Monday night. I’ve tentatively listed them in Schedule C but not included them in the $42.50 total. If you add them, the contribution will rise by $9. Please confirm by 2:00 pm Monday 17 June so I can finalise the stacking diagram.

Given your swift-water training on Saturday morning, I’ve kept you off the Kiln 1 unloading roster on 22 June. I’ve swapped you with Daniel, and you’re now down to help clean and kiln-wash shelves from 6:00–7:30 pm on Sunday 23 June. Let me know if that clashes with the afternoon rescue session you mentioned.

Thanks again for catching the mismatch between the cooling log and v11. The corrected hold is 20 minutes at 1,220°C, followed by the controlled cool to 1,000°C at 80°C per hour.

Best,
Naomi Fletcher
Rivergum Consulting

      "subject": "Re: the costume inventory audit — final reconciliation for 18 June",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve finished the last reconciliation for the costume inventory audit ahead of our 18 June sign-off. The updated file is **Costume_Inventory_Audit_2025-06-16_v7.xlsx**, and I’ve added the supporting photographs and receipts to the folder **Audit Evidence – Final**. This version incorporates the rail-by-rail count you sent on 11 June and Priya’s corrections from Friday.

We now have 1,842 individual items recorded, with 1,796 physically verified. Of the remaining 46, 31 are confirmed as being out on loan for the summer productions, nine are awaiting identification, and six are still unaccounted for. The six missing pieces are the two red military jackets (CJ-044 and CJ-045), the green brocade waistcoat (MW-118), the child’s fox cape (AN-027), and the matching silver dance tunics (DN-203A/B). I checked the old paper issue book as you suggested, but there have been no entries against any of them since the October 2023 production.

The valuation sheet now shows a total replacement value of £68,415. That is £1,260 lower than the figure in version 6 because the three Victorian mourning dresses were duplicated under both “Women’s Period” and “Black Formal.” I removed the duplicate records rather than adjusting the individual values. I also corrected the insurance value of the beaded 1920s gown from £480 to £840, matching the appraisal dated 4 March.

There are two decisions still needed for the final report:

1. Whether to write off the six missing pieces now (£1,475 combined replacement value) or leave them open until the post-production return check on 7 July.
2. Whether the £326 spent on archival boxes and acid-free tissue should be listed as an audit expense or charged to routine wardrobe supplies.

My preference is to leave the missing items open until 7 July and classify the £326 as an audit expense, since the purchases were specifically required to address the storage issues noted during the 29 May inspection. I’ve drafted the report on that basis in **Costume_Audit_Report_Draft_16Jun.docx**, but the relevant paragraphs are highlighted so they’re easy to change.

Could you please review tabs 3 (“Exceptions”) and 6 (“Valuation”) before noon on Wednesday, 18 June? I know you said you’ll be at the upper river gauges early and have rescue training preparations in the evening, so a simple “approved” by email is enough if you don’t have time to add comments. I can then export the signed PDF and send the complete pack to the committee before the 4:00 p.m. deadline.

One final detail: the photograph labelled IMG_7714 is the navy cavalry coat, not the black frock coat. I corrected the filename in the evidence folder, but you may still see the old label if your copy synced before 9:30 this morning.

Thanks again for doing the second count of the accessories cabinet. Finding those 14 feather trims cleared nearly half the discrepancy from the 3 June worksheet.

Best,
Morgan",

      "subject": "Re: the subtitling backlog — final files and remaining corrections",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve finished the last full pass on the subtitling backlog and uploaded the revised files to the shared folder under “Training Videos/Subtitles/Final Review – 18 June”. That clears the six recordings we agreed were still outstanding after your 12 June checklist.

The completed files are:

• SWR-04_River-Hazards_2024-05-11_EN-AU_v3.srt
• SWR-05_Throwbag-Drills_2024-05-11_EN-AU_v4.srt
• SWR-06_Foot-Entrapment_2024-05-18_EN-AU_v3.srt
• SWR-07_Tethered-Swimmer_2024-05-18_EN-AU_v2.srt
• Gauge-Access_Flood-Conditions_2024-05-25_EN-AU_v3.srt
• Debrief_Cedar-Bend_2024-05-25_EN-AU_v2.srt

I used the terminology sheet you sent on 14 June, so “river right”, “river left”, “PFD” and “downstream V” are now consistent throughout. I also replaced “staff gate” with “staff gauge” at 00:07:42 in the Gauge Access video and corrected the Cedar Bend location name at 00:03:19. The automatic transcript had it as “Cedar Ben” in three places.

There are four points I still need you to confirm before I mark everything closed:

1. In SWR-05 at 00:12:08, I hear “ten-metre throw line”, but the equipment list says the yellow bags contain 15-metre lines.
2. In SWR-06 at 00:18:31, the speaker’s name is unclear. I’ve left “[trainer]” rather than guessing between Callum and Colin.
3. In Gauge Access at 00:09:54, you say what sounds like “the Orana telemetry cabinet”. If Orana is the site name, should it be capitalised in the subtitle and added to the glossary?
4. In the Cedar Bend debrief at 00:16:22, the radio call sign sounds like “Rescue Two”, although your notes from 27 May say “Rescue Three”.

I’ve highlighted those captions in the accompanying document, “Subtitle_Query_Log_18-06.xlsx”. If you can add your answers in column F by Thursday, 20 June, I can make the final corrections that evening. There are only 11 caption blocks affected, so it should take less than half an hour once I have your responses.

Timing and reading speed are now within the limits we set: no more than two lines per caption, approximately 42 characters per line, and a target maximum of 20 characters per second. I split the longer safety warning in SWR-04 at 00:21:10 rather than reducing its screen time, as you asked. I also retained “[rushing water]” and the radio tone descriptions where they add useful context, but removed repeated ambient-water labels during continuous sequences.

For tracking purposes, this batch came to 287 finished minutes. Added to the 413 minutes already approved on 6 June, that brings the project total to 700 minutes. There are no unassigned videos left in the backlog folder. The two short clips labelled “Helmet Cam B” and “Boat Ramp Test” remain excluded, in line with your email of 10 June, because they’re reference footage rather than training material.

I’ve attached my invoice for the agreed remaining amount of $516.60, based on 287 minutes at $1.80 per finished minute. No rush on payment before the four queries are resolved; I mainly wanted the figures to match the completion log.

Thanks again for checking the technical wording so carefully. I know you’ve been fitting this around gauge rounds and the weekend rescue sessions, and your timestamped notes have made the final pass much easier.

Kind regards,

Leanne Mercer
Rivergum Realty

      "subject": "Re: the glaze firing schedule – final May kiln slots",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve updated the glaze firing schedule with the changes we agreed after Tuesday’s kiln check. The current version is **Glaze_Firing_Schedule_May_v9.xlsx** in the shared studio folder; please ignore v8, as that still shows your river-gauge callout weekend against the wrong firing.

Your two crates of work are now booked as follows:

• **Thursday 16 May, Kiln 2** — cone 6 oxidation, firing starts at 18:30. This is the 42-litre load with your eight blue-grey bowls, four test tiles and Jo’s six small mugs. I’ve allowed a 20-minute hold at 1200°C, as noted on your firing sheets. Estimated switch-off is 07:15 on Friday 17 May, with unloading no earlier than 16:00.

• **Tuesday 21 May, Kiln 1** — cone 6 oxidation, firing starts at 17:45. This will take the remaining seven bowls, the two lidded jars and your three river-silt glaze tests marked RS-4, RS-5 and RS-6. We’ll use the slower 100–600°C ramp you requested because of the thicker jar bases. Estimated completion is 08:30 on Wednesday 22 May; I’ve marked the kiln closed until 18:00 for cooling.

I moved the larger load off **Saturday 18 May**, since you confirmed you’re teaching the swift-water rescue session that weekend and won’t be able to do the pre-fire shelf check. Priya has taken that slot for her stoneware instead. In return, she’ll help me load Kiln 1 on the 21st, so you won’t need to leave the north gauge run early. If your Tuesday field round overruns, just text me before 16:30; I can check the foot rings and witness cones against the photographs you sent.

The only unresolved item is the RS-6 test. Its label says “cone 6, light reduction,” but both May firings are oxidation. In your message of 6 May you said oxidation was acceptable for this batch, whereas the handwritten note on the pot says to hold it for the June gas firing. I’ve left RS-6 in the green holding tray for now. Please confirm by noon on Monday 20 May whether it should go into the 21 May load or stay out for the **8 June gas firing**.

Costs have also been corrected. The 16 May shared load is **£18.40** for your portion, and the 21 May load is **£24.75**, including the £3.00 slow-ramp surcharge. Your total is therefore **£43.15**, not £46.15 as shown in v8. There’s no additional shelf-wash charge because you supplied the kiln wash last month. You can add the amount to your May studio account rather than transferring it separately.

Could you bring the first crate in by **19:00 on Wednesday 15 May**? Please put the bowls on the lower ware rack, not beside Kiln 2; Helen needs the aisle clear for the electrical inspection at 09:00 Thursday. The second crate can arrive any time before 15:30 on the 21st. I’ve printed the latest copy of **Mara_Ellis_Firing_Sheets_May.pdf** and clipped it to the kiln log, including your note that the blue-grey glaze can run if applied thicker than 1.5 mm.

Assuming RS-6 is settled, I think that finally closes the May schedule. I’ll send you the cone photographs and firing graphs after each kiln has cooled.

Best,
Megan",

      "subject": "Re: the seed-bank accession list — final corrections for 2025 intake",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve finished checking the seed-bank accession list against the paper packets and the freezer inventory. The corrected file is now called “UpperVale_SeedBank_Accession_List_2025-06-18_v12.xlsx”; please use that rather than v11, which still has the duplicated Calder Beck entries we discussed on Monday.

There are 186 accessions in total for the 2025 intake, covering 42 taxa and 17 collection sites. I corrected the collection dates for UVSB-25-071 through UVSB-25-076 from 14 May to 12 May, based on your field sheet from the Rookhope gauge visit. I also changed the grid reference for UVSB-25-103, meadowsweet from East Haugh, to NZ 18462 42791. The previous reference placed it on the opposite bank.

The six Calder Beck packets collected on 29 May were entered twice in v11. I retained UVSB-25-118 through UVSB-25-123 and removed the duplicate block numbered 124–129. The later accession numbers have therefore shifted down by six. This means the final entry, the water avens from Low Wiske collected on 9 June, is UVSB-25-186 rather than UVSB-25-192. I added an “Old provisional ID” column so labels already printed from the 11 June draft can be reconciled without guesswork.

Three items still need your confirmation before I lock the workbook:

1. UVSB-25-044, yellow flag iris, is recorded as 38 g on the envelope but 83 g on “Seed_Collections_April-May_2025.pdf.” I have provisionally used 38 g, as that matches the balance log.
2. UVSB-25-097 and UVSB-25-098 both list River Lune tributary L-4 at gauge marker 2.6 m. Was 098 actually taken at marker 2.9 m, as noted in the margin of your waterproof sheet?
3. The consent form for Fenwick Meadow, dated 7 June, permits collection of up to 250 g. Our combined cleaned weight is 263.4 g across four accessions. You mentioned that 21.8 g was retained by the landowner; if so, I’ll record the deposited quantity as 241.6 g and add that explanation to the notes.

I have also uploaded “Accession_Label_Crosswalk_v3.pdf” and “2025_Intake_Missing_Documents_18Jun.docx” to the shared Seed Bank/2025/Final Review folder. Only two documents remain outstanding: the signed Moor End permission sheet and the photograph of the UVSB-25-152 envelope. If you can send those, along with answers to the three points above, by 16:00 on Friday 20 June, I can issue the locked list before Monday’s freezer audit.

No need to review the germination-priority column again—I incorporated your 16 June comments, including moving the 14 river-corridor accessions into the autumn trial group. I hope Saturday’s rescue-training session leaves you enough time to look at the few remaining queries, but Monday morning is still workable if the river levels keep you out longer than planned.

Thanks again for catching the willowherb identification in the earlier draft.

Best,
Natalie",

      "subject": "Re: 1 July rent increase notice from Hawthorn Lettings",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve gone through the landlord’s 28 April letter, the attached Form 4 and our tenancy agreement again. The notice says the rent for 16 Millbank Terrace will rise from £1,180 to £1,345 per month from 1 July—an increase of £165, or just under 14%. That is the same figure Hawthorn Lettings quoted in their email of 2 May, so at least the paperwork and their message now match. The first version they slipped under the door on 26 April said £1,375, which is why I think we should keep all three documents.

I spoke to Priya at the tenants’ advice line this morning. She said the key issue is not simply whether the increase is steep, but whether the Form 4 was served correctly and whether £1,345 reflects the local market. Our fixed term ended on 31 January and the tenancy became monthly periodic on 1 February, so the landlord can propose an increase under section 13. However, Priya noticed that the form is dated 28 April but states it was served on 30 April. She thinks that probably still gives the required month’s notice for a 1 July start, although she wants to see the envelope and the complete form before confirming.

Could you photograph the envelope when you get home? I put it on the hall table beside the blue folder. Please include the postmark and both sides. I’ve already scanned “Rent Increase Notice – 28 April,” “Form 4 – Proposed New Rent” and the signed tenancy dated 18 January last year. I’ll forward those to Priya this afternoon along with Hawthorn’s 2 May email.

On comparable rents, I found three two-bedroom places within half a mile advertised at £1,250, £1,275 and £1,295. None has the damp patch in the back bedroom or the recurring boiler-pressure fault we reported on 12 February and again on 19 March. I’ve saved the listings as PDFs before they disappear. That should help if we negotiate or refer the proposed rent to the tribunal.

My preference is still to write to Elaine Porter before filing anything. We could offer £1,260 from 1 July, conditional on the bedroom damp being treated and the boiler repair being completed by 15 June. If they refuse, Priya says we must submit the tribunal application before the new rent is due; we should not simply pay the old amount without taking formal action. She also stressed that we should continue paying the current £1,180 in full and on time meanwhile.

I’ve drafted a response headed “Without Prejudice – Proposed Rent Increase at 16 Millbank Terrace,” but I won’t send it until you’ve checked it. I left the draft in the shared folder. Can you read it after your gauge round tomorrow? If you’re on the late callout again, just add comments and I’ll send the final version by noon on Friday, 10 May.

I know this is the last thing you need alongside the river work and Saturday’s rescue training, but we do have grounds to push back calmly. Please don’t ring Elaine from the depot; keeping everything in writing is safer.

Love,
Morgan",

      "subject": "RE: Materials order RB-44718 shipped short – balance confirmed",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve now had written confirmation from our supplier regarding the short shipment against purchase order RB-44718, originally dispatched on 14 August and delivered to the Riverbend depot on 16 August.

As you recorded on the signed delivery docket DD-88164, the consignment contained only 18 of the 24 galvanised gauge-post brackets and 42 of the 50 stainless M10 x 90 mm anchor bolts ordered. The six missing brackets and eight missing bolts were also omitted from packing slip PS-44718-1, although the supplier’s tax invoice INV-70392 charged us for the complete order. The invoiced total was $3,846.70 including GST, of which $684.20 relates to the items that did not arrive.

The supplier has accepted the discrepancy on the basis of your photographs from 16 August and the count sheet you sent through last Friday. They’ve issued credit note CN-11908 for $684.20 against INV-70392 and raised replacement order SO-44718-B at no additional cost. I’ve attached copies of both documents for your records.

The balance is booked to leave their Brisbane warehouse on Tuesday, 3 September, via Northline consignment NGE284771. Their current estimate is delivery to Riverbend between 5 and 6 September. I’ve asked them to label the two cartons “BALANCE OF PO RB-44718 – HOLD FOR MARA ELLIS” so they aren’t combined with the routine stores delivery again. There should be one carton containing the six brackets and a smaller carton containing the eight bolts, together with revised packing slip PS-44718-2.

Could you please check the quantities before signing the carrier’s docket? In particular, the brackets should be the 320 mm hot-dip galvanised type shown on specification sheet GWB-320 Rev C, not the shorter 250 mm version they tried to substitute in July. If either carton is damaged or the count is still wrong, note it on the docket and send me a photo before the driver leaves if practical.

Accounts has put the original invoice on hold rather than paying it less the shortage. Once you confirm that the balance has arrived, I’ll have them apply CN-11908 and release the corrected net amount of $3,162.50. That will keep the PO, goods receipt and invoice aligned in our system.

I appreciate this has held up the bracket replacements planned for the North Fork and Mill Crossing gauge sites. The supplier has agreed to reimburse up to $95 for any additional depot-to-site freight caused by the split delivery, so please retain the transport receipt if you need to make a separate run. There is no need for your team to absorb that cost against the gauge maintenance allocation.

Please let me know when the cartons land, or if the tracking has not updated by the afternoon of 4 September. I’ll chase their dispatch manager directly if there’s another delay.

Kind regards,

Narelle Bishop
Property and Procurement Coordinator
Riverbend Property Services

      "subject": "Re: the glaze firing schedule — revised kiln slots for 18–24 June",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

I’ve updated the glaze firing schedule following your note about the early gauge checks at Broom Weir and your rescue-training weekend. The revised version is attached as “Glaze_Firing_Schedule_18-24_June_v6.xlsx”; please ignore v5, as that still shows you loading Kiln 2 on Saturday morning.

Your 38 pieces are now booked into Kiln 2 for the cone 6 oxidation firing on Tuesday 18 June. I’ve allowed two shelves for the 14 river-stone bowls, three for the 18 blue-grey mugs, and one half-shelf for the six test tiles. If you can leave everything on the labelled trolley by 18:30 on Monday 17 June, I’ll load with Priya that evening. We’re aiming to start the kiln at 07:00 Tuesday, reach cone 6 at roughly 18:30, and unload after 16:00 on Wednesday 19 June once it is below 80°C.

I kept your “Estuary Blue” mugs out of the Thursday 20 June firing, as agreed. That kiln is now nearly full of Ruth’s iron-rich stoneware, and your last test showed the blue crawling when it shared the hotter top shelf. Your six tiles—EB-21 through EB-26—will instead go on shelf 4 in Tuesday’s firing. Please write the glaze combinations on the back in oxide pencil and add them to “Cone6_Test_Log_June.pdf”; EB-24 was missing its second coat in the previous log.

The firing fee comes to £57: £48 for the six-shelf allocation plus £9 for the test-tile space. You already have a £12 credit from the cancelled 7 June firing, so the balance due is £45. There’s no need to transfer it before firing; I’ve put it on the studio account for payment by Friday 28 June.

For the rest of the week, Kiln 1 remains booked for the cone 04 bisque firing at 08:00 on Friday 21 June. I’ve left space for up to 24 of your small training cups if they are bone dry by Thursday evening. The community raku session is still going ahead on Sunday 23 June from 10:00–14:00, but I’ve marked you as unavailable because of the swift-water session. Tom has agreed to cover your 09:30 safety briefing, so you don’t need to come across after training.

One practical point: the replacement thermocouple has arrived, but Kiln 2 is still reading around 8°C high at the controller. I’ll use the witness cones on shelves 2, 4 and 6 and record the actual bend in the firing log. If Tuesday’s reading drifts by more than 15°C, I’ll hold the kiln and message you before changing the programme. The schedule currently specifies a 15-minute soak rather than the 25 minutes we used on 30 May, which should help with the pinholing on the bowls.

Could you confirm by Sunday evening that Monday’s 18:30 drop-off still works? If river levels mean you’re called out, you can leave the trolley key with Dan at reception before 17:00, or I can collect the boxes from your porch after the studio closes.

Thanks,
Leanne",

      ],
      "subject": "Harbour pilot certification renewal – medical accepted and final assessment booking",
      "content": "Hi Mara,

      "content": "Hi,

I have now reconciled the logger export with the handwritten readings for Batch F-0614, the 120 L elderflower-and-ginger ferment that overshot temperature on 16 June. The corrected timeline is in “F-0614_Temperature_Excursion_v7.pdf,” which replaces v6 from Tuesday.

The vessel was pitched at 18.4°C at 19:20 on 14 June. It remained between 18.1°C and 19.6°C until 22:40 on 15 June, then rose steadily after the cooling-loop valve stuck. The probe recorded 24.0°C at 01:50 on 16 June, 27.8°C at 04:10, and a maximum of 29.3°C at 05:35. Your 05:42 manual reading of 29.1°C confirms that the logger was not simply drifting. Once you freed the valve and circulated the two 10 L ice-water containers, the batch fell below 24°C at 08:25 and reached 20.2°C by 13:10. Total time above our 24°C limit was 6 hours 35 minutes, including 2 hours 20 minutes above 27°C.

I also corrected the earlier note about the sugar addition. We added 8.6 kg, not 9.0 kg, giving an original gravity of 1.046. Yesterday’s final gravity was 1.008 in both samples after temperature correction, so attenuation is about 83%. The retained bottle opened normally: no gush, rope, film, or solvent aroma. There is a little more pear/banana ester than in Batch F-0524, but the panel of four did not identify harsh fusel alcohol. pH moved from 4.18 at pitching to 3.36 on 21 June, which is consistent with the previous batches.

Micro results from Northbank came back this morning. The report “NB-24-1887_F0614.pdf” shows no detectable coliforms or enteric organisms, and the yeast morphology is consistent with the production culture. The low-level Lactobacillus signal was also present in the control blank, so the lab has marked it as probable handling contamination rather than evidence of spoilage. I have attached their amended certificate, dated 27 June, along with “F-0614_Sensory_Scores.xlsx.”

On that basis, I agree with your proposal not to dump the full 112 L remaining after sampling. Please keep it quarantined and clearly tagged until we complete the 72-hour package check. I filled twelve 330 mL test bottles at 15:00 today: six will stay at 20°C and six at 30°C. I’ll check pressure, pH, aroma, and visible growth at 24, 48, and 72 hours. If there is no abnormal pressure rise and pH remains within 0.10 of today’s value, we can release it for the volunteer event, but not before Monday, 1 July.

For the root cause, I have changed the wording from “operator failed to monitor” to “cooling valve mechanical seizure compounded by alarm-routing failure.” The alarm did trigger at 24°C, but it went only to the retired tablet in the store room. That matches the notification log you sent. Please confirm that the replacement valve installed on 22 June is the stainless V2 unit, serial CV-4471, and that the high-temperature alert now reaches both your phone and mine. Once confirmed, I’ll close actions 3 and 4 in “CAPA_F-0614_revC.docx.”

Thanks again for getting there at 05:40 after your gauge round. Without the manual check and rapid cooling, we would almost certainly have lost the batch.
